pr_semantic_analysis.change_summary: The unstable Activity element is no longer an alias for the Offscreen element. It now has its own global React symbol and fiber work tag, while delegating its child rendering to Offscreen behavior. Server rendering recognizes it through the existing Offscreen path, and component naming/DevTools now expose it as "Activity".

behavior_changes.description: Callers importing unstable_Activity now receive the distinct react.activity element type instead of react.offscreen, and that new type is accepted as a valid React element type.
evidence: ReactClient changes the exported unstable_Activity identity.
ReactSymbols defines a separate globally registered symbol.
Element-type validation explicitly recognizes the new symbol.

behavior_changes.description: When an Activity element reaches the client reconciler, it receives a dedicated Activity fiber whose children are processed through an Offscreen child fiber using the Activity props' mode and children; its ref is forwarded to that child fiber.

Activity begin-work constructs Offscreen props from mode and children.

local_risks.description: The exported Activity identity changes from react.offscreen to react.activity. If supported consumers compare, cache, serialize, or manually construct the former symbol—or pair this client export with a renderer that does not recognize the new symbol—Activity elements can cease to be interpreted as they were previously.

Client reconciliation introduces a distinct Activity wrapper around an Offscreen fiber, whereas server rendering directly shares Offscreen handling. Hydration and ref behavior should be checked to ensure that this intentionally different internal tree shape remains semantically equivalent.

DevTools correctness now depends on mapping numeric work tag 31 to Activity for the appropriate renderer versions; an incorrect version cutoff could cause Activity fibers to be unknown, mislabeled, or filtered inconsistently.
